title: Record Breakers
intro: The biggest, fastest and tallest things in nature and space. Can you spot the champions?

questions.prompt: What is the tallest mountain on Earth, measured from sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, rises about 8,850 metres above sea level, higher than any other mountain.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest animal known to have ever lived?
questions.explanation: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have lived on Earth, bigger even than the largest dinosaurs.

questions.prompt: Which is the fastest land animal?
questions.explanation: Cheetahs are the fastest land mammals and can reach 60 to 70 miles an hour over short distances.

questions.prompt: Which is the tallest animal alive today?
questions.explanation: Giraffes are the world's tallest mammals. Their legs alone can be taller than many adult people.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet and the one closest to the Sun.

questions.prompt: The emperor penguin is the largest kind of penguin.
questions.explanation: Emperor penguins are the tallest and heaviest of all penguins, standing about 115 centimetres tall.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lizard in the world?
questions.explanation: The Komodo dragon is the biggest lizard alive and can grow up to about 3 metres long.

questions.prompt: A day on Jupiter, one full spin, lasts about how many Earth hours?
questions.explanation: Jupiter spins once about every 10 hours, faster than any other planet, so its days are very short.

questions.prompt: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Venus is the hottest planet. Its thick clouds trap heat, so it is even hotter than Mercury, which is closer to the Sun.

questions.prompt: The African elephant is the largest animal living on land.
questions.explanation: African elephants are the biggest land animals on Earth. Large adults can weigh several tonnes.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest bird alive today?
questions.explanation: The ostrich is the biggest bird on Earth. It can grow taller than a grown-up person, but it is far too heavy to fly.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest rodent in the world?
questions.explanation: The capybara lives in South America and can be as big as a large dog. It loves water and has slightly webbed feet for swimming.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest fish in the sea?
questions.explanation: The whale shark is the biggest fish of all. Despite its size, it eats tiny plankton. The blue whale is bigger, but it is a mammal, not a fish.

questions.prompt: Which animal is the fastest of all when it dives through the air?
questions.explanation: When a peregrine falcon swoops down from high up, it reaches amazing speeds, making it the fastest animal on the planet.

questions.prompt: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara stretches across much of North Africa. It is the largest hot desert, almost as big as the whole of the United States.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest moon in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Ganymede circles Jupiter and is the biggest moon of all. It is even wider than the planet Mercury!

questions.prompt: What is the largest tropical rainforest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon rainforest covers a huge part of South America and is home to an incredible number of plants and animals.

questions.prompt: Which kind of tree grows the tallest?
questions.explanation: Coast redwoods grow in California and can grow more than 100 metres tall, higher than a 30-storey building.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest reptile alive today?
questions.explanation: Saltwater crocodiles are the biggest reptiles on Earth. Large males can grow longer than a family car.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest of the great apes?
questions.explanation: Gorillas are the biggest apes. A grown male gorilla can weigh more than two adult people put together, yet gorillas mostly munch on plants.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest member of the deer family?
questions.explanation: The moose is the biggest deer of all. A large male can weigh as much as a small car, and its antlers can be wider than a door.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the highest waterfall in the world, found in Venezuela?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops almost a kilometre. The water falls so far that much of it turns to mist before it reaches the bottom.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Even though it is called a sea, the Caspian Sea is a lake surrounded by land. It is the largest lake on Earth by area.

questions.prompt: What is the largest single object in our solar system?
questions.explanation: The Sun is by far the biggest thing in our solar system. It is so huge that about a million Earths could fit inside it.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Greenland is the largest island. Australia is bigger, but it is counted as a continent rather than an island.

questions.prompt: The tallest volcano in our solar system, Olympus Mons, is on which planet?
questions.explanation: Olympus Mons on Mars is about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest. It is the biggest volcano we know of.

questions.prompt: Antarctica counts as the largest desert on Earth.
questions.explanation: A desert is a place that gets very little rain or snow, not just somewhere hot. Antarctica is so dry that it is the biggest desert of all.

questions.prompt: The lion is the largest kind of wild cat.
questions.explanation: Lions are big, but tigers are bigger. The tiger is the largest wild cat in the world.

questions.prompt: An ostrich can run at about how many kilometres per hour?
questions.explanation: Ostriches cannot fly, but their long, strong legs let them run at about 70 kilometres per hour, faster than any other bird on land.

questions.prompt: The Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system, stretches for about how many kilometres?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef runs for about 2,300 kilometres along the coast of Australia. It is so big that it can be seen from space.
